page_title: OpenVoiceFlow — Free Forever, Private by Design

summary.name: OpenVoiceFlow
summary.one_liner: OpenVoiceFlow is a free, open-source, push-to-talk dictation app for macOS that transcribes speech on-device with WhisperKit and pastes the text into any app.
use_cases: Dictating text into any Mac app by holding a key
Writing emails or documents faster than typing
Private transcription without sending audio to the cloud
Dictation offline or in airplane mode
summary.what_it_does: The app is a push-to-talk dictation tool: you hold a key, speak, release, and the transcribed text is pasted into the active app. Audio transcription runs on-device using Whisper models (from tiny to large) via WhisperKit. An optional AI cleanup step is off by default and, when enabled, can use OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, or local Ollama with the user's own API key. It includes a personal dictionary for names and jargon, and settings and history are stored locally in Application Support, with API keys kept in the macOS Keychain. The source code is published on GitHub.
notable: On-device Whisper transcription; audio never leaves the Mac
Source published on GitHub under a project license
AI cleanup is off by default and bring-your-own-key when enabled
Anonymous aggregate usage counters can be disabled in Settings > Privacy
caveats: Intel Macs work but the page says smaller models are recommended for them
AI cleanup, if enabled, sends text to the chosen model provider and requires the user's own API key
The app shares anonymous aggregate usage counters unless the user turns them off
